## Check a resolver change before it merges, and see what is still unsettled

Both consumers decide tonnages from this package, so every change runs the parity report before it merges -- it reads each consumer's resolver out of its git object store at a pinned ref, never a working tree, and exit 1 is a disagreement or a comparison it could not establish (neither is a pass). It needs ../fsg-tender-review and ../fsg-bluebeam-steel-standards checked out. The known-issues run reports and never gates: it prints OBSERVED beside EXPECTED so the open estimator questions cannot quietly outlive their subject.

| Run | What it does | Defined in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `python tools/known_issues.py` | Run the reproducers for the open issues the consolidation turned up. | `tools/known_issues.py` |
| `python tools/parity_report.py` | Prove `fsg_common.sections` answers what both source resolvers answer. | `tools/parity_report.py` |

## Regenerate the packaged section library from the estimating workbook

The section library and labour rates are a generated snapshot of the workbook's 90_Lists -- never hand-edit data/fsg_sections.json; change the workbook and re-run this. --check re-reads the workbook and compares the content hash, which is the only thing that answers whether the copy still matches; an age threshold cannot. Read-only against the workbook, and a merge here changes nothing downstream until each consumer moves its pin.

| Run | What it does | Defined in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `python scripts/refresh_from_workbook.py` | Regenerate the packaged copy of the FSG section library and labour rates. | `scripts/refresh_from_workbook.py` |
